targets.title: Heuristics and biases in charity
targets.evidence_quote: We conducted a very close replication and extension of four studies reported in Baron & Szymanska [ 2 ].
targets.outcome_quote: Our replication results were consistent with the original findings; we found support for each of our replication and extension hypotheses, though we suggest caution with interpreting the findings of hypothesis 5 (forced charity/government taxes; further elaborated below in the ‘Limitations’ section).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly confirm the replicated finding; the overall verdict governs the Baron and Szymanska target.

targets.authors: Gneezy U , Keenan EA , Gneezy A
targets.title: Avoiding overhead aversion in charity
targets.evidence_quote: Hypothesis 7, which found that participants were biased towards a charity where overhead is paid for by another donor even when cost-effectiveness is kept constant, acts as a conceptual replication of Gneezy et al . [ 16 ].
targets.outcome_quote: Hypothesis 7, which found that participants were biased towards a charity where overhead is paid for by another donor even when cost-effectiveness is kept constant, acts as a conceptual replication of Gneezy et al . [ 16 ]. In contrast to the between-subject design that they used in their study, our extension shows that this effect occurs in a within-subject context as well.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly confirm the replicated finding; the overall verdict governs the Baron and Szymanska target.

reasoning: New samples retest four studies in one published chapter, plus an explicitly identified conceptual replication in the overhead-funding extension. Other reputation citations motivate a new donation-choice hypothesis or contextualize its results; their distinct donation-amount findings were not specifically retested. The overall successful verdict on the chapter takes priority over individual contrasts and validity caveats.
